note: Four N-terminal/conformational anti-tau antibodies cut tau in P301L/P301S mice and all failed in biomarker-confirmed prodromal-to-mild AD despite real engagement of N-terminal tau.
label: Alzheimer's (anti-tau)

engagement.model: P301S (PS19) tau-transgenic mice + seeding biosensor assay
engagement.note: HJ8.5, tilavonemab's parent, was picked for blocking P301S-lysate seeding in a biosensor assay, then infused into P301S mouse ventricles.
engagement.short: Parent antibody blocks seeding, infused ICV
engagement.quote: Using a cell-based biosensor assay, we screened anti-tau monoclonal antibodies for their ability to block seeding activity present in P301S brain lysates.
engagement.judgement: Opens the engagement strip at the first published use of the seeding/P301S system for an antibody that became a clinical candidate (HJ8.5 -> ABBV-8E12/tilavonemab).

engagement.note: Systemic tau rose after dosing in tau-transgenic mice, monkeys and humans; AD participants rose more than healthy controls.
engagement.short: Plasma tau rose in mice and humans
engagement.quote: Semorinemab also showed clear evidence of target engagement in vivo, with increases in systemic tau concentrations observed in tau transgenic mice, nonhuman primates, and humans.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level only (Science paywall, no PMC). Same paper puts mouse, monkey and phase 1 human PD side by side, so comparison_stated=true; subjects mixed (healthy controls + mild-to-moderate AD). Mouse efficacy used murine surrogates; whether the mouse PD read-out used semorinemab itself is not stated, so product_in_model=null. Phase 1 NCT02820896 has no posted results.

engagement.model: Tau-transgenic mouse interstitial fluid (N-terminal tau removal)
engagement.note: Gosuranemab cleared 80–93% of unbound N-terminal tau from patient CSF, as it had from mouse interstitial fluid.
engagement.quote: Treatment with gosuranemab was associated with a robust reduction in the CSF levels of unbound N-terminal tau, confirming the target engagement of this antibody.
engagement.reason: N-terminal tau engaged as mice predicted
engagement.judgement: Status unchanged (same -> same) but added because it is a patients-only, same-paper comparison (TANGO, NCT03352557). Shulman argues N-terminal engagement may miss the seeding-competent, microtubule-binding-region species; that is scored under efficacy, not here. Fleisher 2024 notes zagotenemab showed no direct biomarker evidence of central engagement of aggregated tau, so engagement of the pathological species remains unproven for the conformational antibody.

dose.model: Exposure modeling of extracellular-tau binding (basis unpublished)
dose.note: The 4500-mg dose came from exposure modeling of extracellular-tau binding; no model-derived occupancy target was ever compared with patients.
dose.short: Dose from exposure model, never checked
dose.quote: More participants were allocated to the placebo and 4500-mg semorinemab arms to increase the power of comparisons between these groups, as preliminary exposure modeling suggested sufficient binding of extracellular tau species at the 4500-mg dose.
dose.judgement: Year is the publication of the statement, not the 2017 trial design; the modeling itself is unpublished so model_first_use_year is null. Fleisher 2024 likewise says zagotenemab phase 2 doses rested on nonclinical and phase 1 PK/PD, then reports no direct biomarker evidence of central target engagement. Gosuranemab's TANGO engagement matched its phase 1 (human-to-human), which is not a preclinical-model comparison.

efficacy.note: MC1, zagotenemab's parent, and PHF1 cut tau pathology in JNPL3 mice and delayed motor decline in P301S mice.
efficacy.short: Anti-tau antibodies cut tau in mutant mice
efficacy.quote: We show that peripheral administration of two antibodies against pathological Tau forms significantly reduces biochemical Tau pathology in the JNPL3 mouse model.
efficacy.judgement: First published passive anti-tau antibody efficacy in tau-transgenic mice by a sponsor (Lilly) whose antibody (MC1 -> LY3303560/zagotenemab) reached phase 2; Fleisher 2024 cites exactly these JNPL3/P301S results as the preclinical basis.

efficacy.model: P301L tau-transgenic mice (4R tau, murine surrogate)
efficacy.note: Murine semorinemab cut tau in P301L mice; semorinemab moved neither CDR-SB nor tau-PET in 422 prodromal-to-mild AD patients.
efficacy.short: Mouse tau reduction not replicated in Tauriel
efficacy.quote: It remains uncertain why the preclinical efficacy of the murine surrogate of semorinemab for reducing tau accumulation was not replicated in the Tauriel study.
efficacy.judgement: Authors' own explanations: the N-terminal epitope may be absent from the tau species that spread in early AD, and the P301L model overexpresses 4R tau versus mixed 3R/4R in AD. Tauriel NCT03289143, results posted 2022-03-16.

efficacy.note: All four antibodies cut tau in P301L/P301S mice and all failed in early AD; authors call the models unsuitable for extracellular-tau drugs.
efficacy.short: Four mouse successes, four clinical failures
efficacy.quote: However, similar to gosuranemab, these agents have failed to demonstrate a clear clinical benefit in patients with early AD, calling into question the predictive value of these mouse studies for clinical efficacy.
efficacy.reason: Mice cut tau; patients did not
efficacy.judgement: Second contra entry kept because it is the class-wide, explicit model-vs-patient statement: FTD-mutant 4R mice model intraneuronal aggregation, not extracellular spread, so are 'unsuitable for testing therapeutics aimed at intercepting extracellular tau'; N-terminal epitopes may not capture the microtubule-binding-region seeds, which are scarce in CSF. Florian 2023 (tilavonemab, Brain) adds that N-terminal antibodies miss truncated tau that mid-domain antibodies detect. product_in_model null: gosuranemab's own ISF data are cited as gosuranemab, but the other three used murine surrogates.

safety.model: Nonhuman primates and tau-transgenic mice (PK/PD; tox species not stated in abstract)
safety.note: Mice and monkeys were dosed for PK/engagement; no published comparison of a tox-model prediction with the clean Phase 1–2 safety.
safety.short: Clean in patients; no model comparison
safety.quote: No concerning safety signals were observed in the phase 1 clinical trial at single doses up to 16,800 mg and multiple doses totaling 33,600 mg in a month.
safety.judgement: Abstract-level; the toxicology species and findings are not in the abstract and no FDA review exists (nothing approved). All four phase 2 trials reported acceptable safety; zagotenemab had more AEs (85.1% vs 74.6%) with no attributable category (Fleisher 2024), which is not a model contradiction.
